issues.legal_issue: When clauses in a will are inconsistent, the later clause prevails only when the clauses cannot be reconciled.
material_facts: The will first bequeathed the Schedule A properties to the testator’s sister’s son, and a later recital provided that those properties were to be possessed and enjoyed as Tavazhi.
The petitioner argued that the earlier bequest created an absolute estate and that the High Court should not have relied on the later recital.
The Supreme Court found no infirmity in the High Court’s judgment and dismissed the special leave petition.
issues.conclusion: An irreconcilable later clause in a will prevails over an earlier clause; that rule applies only when the clauses cannot be reconciled. The Court found no infirmity in the High Court’s interpretation and dismissed the special leave petition.
issues.legal_principle: Section 88 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 provides that where two clauses or gifts in a will are irreconcilable, the last prevails, reflecting the maxim that the last intention expressed in a will governs. The rule applies only where the clauses cannot be reconciled (Rameswar v. Balraj, AIR 1935 PC 187). The Court also referred to Harimond v. Treharne, [1938] 3 All ER 308, and to Ramachandra Shenoy v. Hilda Brite, AIR 1964 SC 1323; Navneet Lal v. Gokul, AIR 1976 SC 794; and Ramakrishorelal v. Kamalnarayan, AIR 1963 SC 890, concerning interpretation of wills and ascertaining testamentary intention.

predicates.will_interpretation_challenge: A party challenges a court’s interpretation of clauses in a will.
predicates.two_will_clauses_irreconcilable: Two clauses in the will express dispositions that cannot be reconciled.
predicates.later_will_clause_controls: The later clause in the will governs over the earlier inconsistent clause.

issues.definition: When a will is under interpretation and its clauses cannot be reconciled, the later clause governs.
